name: Medicine shortages
summary: UK pharmacists say shortages hit up to 6.4m prescription items a month in 2026; no widespread rationing reported
state: On 17 Nov the National Pharmacy Association estimated that shortages could have affected up to 6.4 million prescription items a month in 2026, based on 14 government supply notifications; the government granted 245 price concessions in October after a record 254 in July (Pharmaceutical Journal). Shortages of several medicines persist across countries, but searches on 24 Nov found no widespread rationing or cancelled treatment across major health systems, so Watch holds.
for_you: People on long-term generic medicines are most likely to meet delays or substitutions at the pharmacy. The NHS advises ordering repeat prescriptions in good time and asking a pharmacist about alternatives.
rubric_hit: Watch: shortages of essential medicines across several countries (UK up to 6.4m items/month); no widespread rationing

sources.title: Pharmaceutical Journal — NPA urges government action on medicines shortages

why: Shipping disruption, factory failures and export curbs can leave essential medicines short, as with US IV fluids after Hurricane Helene in 2024.
drivers: Manufacturing concentrated in India and China, shipping, raw materials, demand spikes, regulation.

rubric.alert: Shortages forcing widespread rationing or cancelled treatment across major health systems.
rubric.watch: A shortage of an essential medicine or supply across several countries, or a UK Serious Shortage Protocol for a widely used medicine.
rubric.normal: No widespread shortages of essential medicines in major health systems.
